title: Khadija's Kitchen
intro: A full identity for a small family-run kitchen selling traditional Dagestani food, from the shop sign down to the dumpling boxes. Clean enough to grow with them, warm enough to still feel like someone's home.
brief: A popular local kitchen was expanding its menu and its line of homemade semi-finished foods, and planning a proper storefront. They needed one identity to carry the products, the shop and their social media, clean without losing the warmth of food made by hand. The packaging came with a practical constraint: it had to print cheaply, through the suppliers they already worked with.
did: I built the logo around the idea of home. The name is stacked into a compact, slightly irregular block of letters, with a small house tucked into the Д, set inside a warm circular frame with dumplings resting at its base. Earthy browns and simple, hand-made shapes keep it approachable rather than corporate.

From there the system rolled out across everything a customer touches: exterior signage, the interior, promotional materials, staff uniforms and the food packaging. For the packaging I designed within what their existing suppliers could print affordably, so the identity had to hold up in flat, simple applications instead of leaning on expensive finishes.
coverAlt: Hanging round shop sign with the Khadija's Kitchen logo: stacked Cyrillic lettering in brown inside a circular frame, with dumplings at its base
